selected.name: Planned Parenthood of the Rocky Mountains
selected.comparativeReason: Direct reproductive/STI care is a distinct preventive-health mechanism worth comparing with general clinics, but multistate and traveling-patient dilution keeps it below concentrated local access candidates.
selected.decisiveQuestion: Quantify marginal effective care for MSA residents and patient health/autonomy, not avoided births as benefits; separate clinical c3 spending from action affiliates and reimbursed care.
selected.concreteFalsifier: Falsified if gifts mainly subsidize services otherwise reimbursed or benefit mostly out-of-MSA traveling patients.
selected.wholeOrganizationScope: Whole multistate affiliate includes clinical, education, advocacy and assistance activities; no single-clinic restricted gift assumed.
selected.independentFinding: PPRM's primary Park Hill/locations evidence establishes Denver clinical services despite blocked Denver Central page. Whole multistate recipient EIN84-0404253; reproductive-care reimbursement and donor effects untested.

selected.name: Tennyson Center for Children
selected.comparativeReason: PCIT and trauma-focused community care supply a specific clinical test, rather than generic youth enrichment; ranked lower because day-treatment/school costs and reimbursement may dominate whole-recipient margin.
selected.decisiveQuestion: Assess all-entrant child behavior/trauma effects and added access beyond Medicaid, with full school/day-treatment costs; distinguish fast referral response from completed treatment.
selected.concreteFalsifier: Actual clinical effect, waitlist access and non-Medicaid marginal capacity may be weak; compare to existing reimbursed care.
selected.wholeOrganizationScope: Whole school/day-treatment/community portfolio statewide, not only PCIT.
selected.independentCohort: Child, perinatal and family clinical care
selected.independentFinding: Tennyson's current community PCIT/family work explicitly includes these counties plus excluded northern counties. Whole Colorado Christian Home/Tennyson EIN61-1458290, including intensive services and administration.

alternates.name: Legal Aid Foundation of Colorado (supporting Colorado Legal Services)
alternates.reason: Broad civil legal aid remains plausible, but recipient-to-CLS whole-cost bridge and health attribution make it a lower immediate priority than Spark.

alternates.name: Atlantis Community
alternates.comparativeReason: First alternate: potentially large daily-function and autonomy gains from community transitions, but donation-sensitive service mix and safe care after transition less clear than direct repairs.
alternates.decisiveQuestion: How many additional safe transitions or accessibility supports occur because of new gifts beyond mandated support, and what sustained function/quality-of-life gain follows?
alternates.concreteFalsifier: Falsified if transitions lack safe adequate care or gifts merely replace mandated/public supports.
alternates.wholeOrganizationScope: Whole recipient includes advocacy, peer support, referrals, youth services and mobile outreach.

alternates.name: Ensight Skills Center
alternates.comparativeReason: Low-vision rehabilitation may produce durable function gains with modest devices/training; alternate because unrestricted activity appears geographically dispersed and metro share uncertain.
alternates.decisiveQuestion: Verify Denver-resident completed rehabilitation and incremental function beyond covered alternatives; exclude Northern Colorado/Boulder despite shared branding and referrals.
alternates.concreteFalsifier: Falsified if recipients would obtain equivalentcoveredcare or most gifts fundout-of-MSAservices.
alternates.wholeOrganizationScope: Whole Ensight includes Northern Colorado and Curtis Strong Center; exclude Boulder/Weld/Larimer benefits.

alternates.name: Inner City Health
alternates.comparativeReason: Strong local integrated-care alternate if Doctors Care/Tepeyac fail donor-additionality tests; not selected simultaneously because similar mechanisms already represented, not because evidence is weak.
alternates.decisiveQuestion: Can new gifts produce high-benefit untreated cases at lower full incremental cost than other local clinics after coverage expansion and existing charity care?
alternates.concreteFalsifier: Falsified if clinic care merely shifts from other providers or expansion does not add clinical capacity.
alternates.wholeOrganizationScope: Whole faith-based recipient includes medical, dental, behavioral and operational/capital costs.

alternates.name: SafeHouse Denver
alternates.comparativeReason: Acute protection from recurrent violence has substantial potential; alternate to Blue Bench's more directly measurable therapy because shelter costs and equivalent capacity require clearer comparison.
alternates.decisiveQuestion: Do marginal funded stays avert actual exposure and improve durable safety beyond available shelters, with full housing cost and trauma outcomes included?
alternates.concreteFalsifier: Falsified if support does not reduce exposure or improve mental health beyond available alternatives.
alternates.wholeOrganizationScope: Whole agency includes shelter occupancy, counseling, advocacy and education, not only hotline costs.

alternates.name: Project Angel Heart
alternates.comparativeReason: Targeted serious-illness meals offer stronger clinical linkage than general pantry distribution, but production/delivery cost and food substitution keep it behind benefits-access candidates.
alternates.decisiveQuestion: Does recipient-matched evidence show sustained health improvement beyond existing food/caregivers, after metro allocation, reimbursement and full meal costs?
alternates.concreteFalsifier: Falsified if meals replace adequate existing food/support or claimed utilization changes lack causal controls.
alternates.wholeOrganizationScope: Full statewide meal production, delivery, advocacy and operations; exclude Boulder/Larimer/Pueblo and other non-MSA recipients.

alternates.name: Rocky Mountain Human Services
alternates.comparativeReason: Specialized I/DD crisis support addresses high need and may avert costly harmful crises; alternate because statutory case-management contracts may dominate philanthropic margin.
alternates.decisiveQuestion: What incremental START prevention or transition work can gifts add beyond county/Medicaid obligations, and does it improve actual crisis/function outcomes?
alternates.concreteFalsifier: Measure crisis/hospital reduction and new capacity enabled by gifts beyond county/Medicaid contracts.
alternates.wholeOrganizationScope: Whole RMHS including long-term care, early intervention, housing and veterans services statewide.

alternates.name: Colorado Center for the Blind
alternates.comparativeReason: Potentially durable daily-living independence is valuable, but residential rehabilitation may be expensive and attract nonmetro students; retain as alternative functional-health comparator.
alternates.decisiveQuestion: What fraction of incremental trainees are MSA residents, what function gains persist relative to vocational-rehab alternatives, and what is full residential cost?
alternates.concreteFalsifier: Falsified if training mostly serves out-of-MSA residents, duplicates vocational-rehab funding or fails to improve sustained functioning.
alternates.wholeOrganizationScope: Full residential/nonresidential training, enrichment, youth and professional education portfolio; resident origin not established by clinic location.

alternates.name: Disability Justice
alternates.comparativeReason: Systemic community-care enforcement has high upside, but statutory funding, implementation and metro attribution are less clear than selected consumer-health/legal candidates.
alternates.decisiveQuestion: Confirm current renamed legal recipient, new donation-sensitive enforcement work and actual safe community-care gains for MSA residents—not settlement promises alone.
alternates.concreteFalsifier: Settlement compliance or appropriate care capacity fails, attribution is small, or transitions worsen safety.
alternates.wholeOrganizationScope: Whole statewide protection/advocacy body covers multiple disabilities, institutions and legal issues; not every legal win is a health gain.

alternates.name: SungateKids
alternates.comparativeReason: Child protection in southern/eastern MSA broadens access beyond Denver CAC, but health consequences of investigative work are less directly established than selected trauma treatment.
alternates.decisiveQuestion: Does additional interview/advocacy capacity improve protective placement or therapy and reduce recurrent abuse beyond public response; exclude Lincoln and obsolete judicial boundaries?
alternates.concreteFalsifier: Falsified if investigative outputs do not improve protection/treatment or prevention education has no measured effect.
alternates.wholeOrganizationScope: Whole organization includes justice-system coordination and education, not only treatment.

alternates.name: Judi's House
alternates.comparativeReason: Specialized bereavement support could prevent persistent severe distress in children, but spontaneous recovery and national research allocation make value less certain than access-focused therapy funds.
alternates.decisiveQuestion: For high-risk bereaved children, are improvements greater and more durable than natural recovery/alternative support, including noncompleters and JAG research/training costs?
alternates.concreteFalsifier: Falsified if most grief resolves similarly without care or observed improvements lack controls/durability.
alternates.wholeOrganizationScope: Whole Judi's House/JAG Institute includes national research/training, not just local counseling.

comparativeCohorts.name: Overdose and recovery
comparativeCohorts.independentComparativeReason: HRAC and CHN have more direct severe-risk supply/clinical pathways than fitness, peer support or abstinence housing. Broader recovery providers face selection, medication-access and reimbursement uncertainty; closed Hornbuckle scholarships cannot underpin marginal claims.

comparativeCohorts.name: Clinical mental health access
comparativeCohorts.independentComparativeReason: Second Wind and Maria Droste offer targeted barrier removal; Spark adds volunteer licensed therapy after legal identity resolution. Jefferson mobile MAT reaches explicit rural gaps. Broad reimbursed providers and nonclinical grief/peer/policy portfolios have more uncertain donor-sensitive clinical reach.

comparativeCohorts.name: Primary, dental and preventive care
comparativeCohorts.independentComparativeReason: Tepeyac and Doctors Care focus underserved access; KIND and Dental Lifeline offer narrower dental mechanisms and volunteer leverage; immunization and reproductive access retain serious preventive hypotheses. STRIDE, Inner City, DIHFS, Clinica, Corvida and CAAH remain credible but broad portfolio/substitution or less resolved marginal paths reduce current research priority.

comparativeCohorts.name: Food and financial access
comparativeCohorts.independentComparativeReason: Hunger Free and Benefits in Action may unlock existing benefit budgets with fewer donated dollars. Meals and food rescue remain serious alternatives, especially medically tailored meals, but food volumes, in-kind valuations and broad goods portfolios are weak substitutes for incremental health.

comparativeCohorts.name: Safe homes and elder support
comparativeCohorts.independentComparativeReason: Energy Outreach and Rebuilding Together offer relatively specific thermal/safety repair hypotheses. Housing systems, disability services and elder supports have larger portfolios or public financing; Chanda alternative-therapy effects are especially uncertain. Rural county representation alone is not a selection reason.

comparativeCohorts.name: Coverage and legal health pathways
comparativeCohorts.independentComparativeReason: CCHI is selected for specific insurance/affordability pathways. LAF/CLS is a credible alternate but broad civil-law funding creates an extra cost/impact bridge; Spark takes its slot. Disability and worker-rights advocacy have plausible high upside but less direct present health conversion.

comparativeCohorts.name: Child, perinatal and family clinical care
comparativeCohorts.independentComparativeReason: Denver CAC, Savio, Tennyson and Thriving Families offer trauma-focused/home-based/perinatal hypotheses worth clinical review. Others combine education, childcare, intensive beds or broad prevention; whole-provider comparisons are essential. Claimed RCT and model labels are leads, not accepted effectiveness.

comparativeCohorts.name: Survivor and homelessness support
comparativeCohorts.independentComparativeReason: Blue Bench offers explicit sexual-trauma therapy across a verified service area. Shelter, basic-needs and justice-center peers are valuable alternatives, but housing counterfactuals and partner attribution make their unrestricted-gift health pathways less resolved.

comparativeCohorts.name: Policy and violence prevention
comparativeCohorts.independentComparativeReason: Bicycle Colorado, Cultivando and Struggle of Love preserve distinct potentially leveraged road-injury, air-exposure and violence mechanisms. Each requires causal policy/violence counterfactuals and whole-recipient costs; none is selected merely for reported contacts or coalition size.

comparativeCohorts.name: Cancer financial and psychosocial support
comparativeCohorts.independentComparativeReason: All three are actual distinct recipients with statewide eligibility. Current limited grants/waitlists and the gap from financial relief to incremental treatment/health place them below selected benefits/coverage and clinical-access candidates, not outside discovery.
